title: Whether a top-level class can be private or protected
answer: No. A top-level Java class can be `public` or package-private (no access modifier), but it cannot be declared `private` or `protected`. `private` and `protected` are meaningful for members and nested types because an enclosing or inheritance relationship exists; a top-level type has no enclosing class. A source file can contain one public top-level class matching the filename plus additional package-private top-level types.
